en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Ninth Chapter
The Discussion on Possession of the Past and Future.
Is one possessed of the past? Yes.
Is it not the case that the past has ceased, has vanished, has changed, has come to an end, and has utterly passed away?
Yes, it is so.
If the past has indeed ceased, vanished, changed, come to an end, and utterly passed away, then surely you should not say:
“One who is endowed with the past”:
is he also endowed with the future?
Yes, he is.
Is it not the case that the future is unborn, unbecome, unarisen, unproduced, unmanifested, and non-apparent?
Yes, it is.
If the future is unborn, unbecome, unarisen, unproduced, unmanifested, and non-apparent, then indeed, you must not say: [that the future exists].
“Endowed with the future.
Is one endowed with the past aggregate of form, endowed with the future aggregate of form, and endowed with the present aggregate of form?
Yes.
Is one possessed of three aggregates of form?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is one possessed of the five past aggregates, possessed of the five future aggregates, and possessed of the five present aggregates?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is one endowed with fifteen aggregates?
One should not say so …pe… .
Is one possessed of the past eye-base, possessed of the future eye-base, and possessed of the present eye-base?
Yes. Is one possessed of all three eye-bases?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that one is possessed of the twelve bases of the past, possessed of the twelve bases of the future, and possessed of the twelve bases of the present?
Yes.
“Is one endowed with the thirty-six bases?
One should not say so … [and so on] … “Is one endowed with the past eye-element, endowed with the future eye-element, and endowed with the present eye-element?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is one endowed with three eye-elements?
One should not say so …pe…
Is one endowed with the eighteen elements of the past, endowed with the eighteen elements of the future, and endowed with the eighteen elements of the present?
Yes. Is one then endowed with fifty-four elements?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one possessed of the eye-faculty of the past, possessed of the eye-faculty of the future, and possessed of the eye-faculty of the present? Yes.
Is one endowed with three eye-faculties?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is one endowed with twenty-two faculties in the past, endowed with twenty-two faculties in the future, and endowed with twenty-two faculties in the present?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is one endowed with sixty-six faculties?
You should not say so… [and so on].
Is it not to be said that one is possessed of the past and the future?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that there exists one who is a meditator on the eight liberations, who obtains the four jhānas at will, and who is a possessor of the nine successive attainments?
Yes, that is so.
If indeed there exists one who is a meditator on the eight liberations, who obtains the four jhānas at will, and who is a possessor of the nine successive attainments, then, indeed, it must be said:
“Endowed with the past and the future.
The discussion on the past, future, and present is finished.
The ninth chapter.
Its summary verse:
For one who sees the benefits, there is the abandoning of the fetters; the fetter has the deathless as its object; form has an object;
the underlying tendencies are without an object; likewise is knowledge; consciousness has the past and future as its object; all consciousness is accompanied by applied thought.
For one who is entirely engaged in initial application and sustained application of thought, sound is the outflow of such thought;
bodily action is not like speech, which follows the mind, for it is likewise [conditioned] by what has passed and what is yet to come.
